passages.text: Ahaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem sixteen years. And unlike David his father, he did not do what was right in the eyes of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Ahaz became king when he was twenty years old.
Ahaz ruled in Jerusalem for sixteen years.
Ahaz did not do what was right in the eyes of the LORD.
David, his ancestor, did what was right in the eyes of the LORD.
Ahaz did not follow David’s example.
passages.original: בֶּן־ עֶשְׂרִ֤ים שָׁנָה֙ אָחָ֣ז בְּמָלְכ֔וֹ וְשֵׁשׁ־ עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְלֹא־ עָשָׂ֧ה הַיָּשָׁ֛ר בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה כְּדָוִ֥יד אָבִֽיו׃

passages.text: Instead, he walked in the ways of the kings of Israel and even made cast images of the Baals.
passages.sermon:
Ahaz was king of Judah.
Ahaz did not follow the LORD like David did.
Ahaz acted like the kings of Israel.
Ahaz copied their ways.
Ahaz made cast images.
Ahaz made these images for the Baals.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֕לֶךְ בְּדַרְכֵ֖י מַלְכֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְגַ֧ם מַסֵּכ֛וֹת עָשָׂ֖ה לַבְּעָלִֽים׃

passages.text: Moreover, Ahaz burned incense in the Valley of Hinnom and sacrificed his sons in the fire, according to the abominations of the nations that the LORD had driven out before the Israelites.
passages.sermon:
Ahaz was king in Jerusalem.
Ahaz did not do what was right in the eyes of the LORD.
Ahaz burned incense in the Valley of Hinnom.
Ahaz sacrificed his sons in the fire.
He did these things like the nations that the LORD had driven out before the Israelites.
These actions were abominations to the LORD.
passages.original: וְה֥וּא הִקְטִ֖יר בְּגֵ֣יא בֶן־ הִנֹּ֑ם וַיַּבְעֵ֤ר אֶת־ בָּנָיו֙ בָּאֵ֔שׁ כְּתֹֽעֲבוֹת֙ הַגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁר֙ הֹרִ֣ישׁ יְהוָ֔ה מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: And he sacrificed and burned incense on the high places, on the hills, and under every green tree.
passages.sermon:
Ahaz was king of Judah.
Ahaz did evil things.
He offered sacrifices at the high places.
He burned incense on the hills.
He worshiped under every green tree.
passages.original: וַיְזַבֵּ֧חַ וַיְקַטֵּ֛ר בַּבָּמ֖וֹת וְעַל־ הַגְּבָע֑וֹת וְתַ֖חַת כָּל־ עֵ֥ץ רַעֲנָֽן׃

passages.text: So the LORD his God delivered Ahaz into the hand of the king of Aram, who attacked him and took many captives to Damascus. Ahaz was also delivered into the hand of the king of Israel, who struck him with great force.
passages.sermon:
Ahaz was king of Judah.
Ahaz did evil in the sight of the LORD.
The LORD was Ahaz’s God.
The LORD delivered Ahaz into the hand of the king of Aram.
The king of Aram attacked Ahaz.
The king of Aram took many captives from Ahaz’s people.
The king of Aram brought the captives to Damascus.
The LORD also delivered Ahaz into the hand of the king of Israel.
The king of Israel struck Ahaz with great force.
passages.original: וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֜הוּ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָיו֮ בְּיַ֣ד מֶ֣לֶךְ אֲרָם֒ וַיַּ֨כּוּ־ ב֔וֹ וַיִּשְׁבּ֤וּ מִמֶּ֙נּוּ֙ שִׁבְיָ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֔ה וַיָּבִ֖יאוּ דַּרְמָ֑שֶׂק וְ֠גַם בְּיַד־ מֶ֤לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ נִתָּ֔ן וַיַּךְ־ בּ֖וֹ מַכָּ֥ה גְדוֹלָֽה׃ס

passages.text: For in one day Pekah son of Remaliah killed 120,000 valiant men in Judah. This happened because they had forsaken the LORD, the God of their fathers.
passages.sermon:
Pekah was the son of Remaliah.
He was the king of Israel.
He attacked the people of Judah.
He killed 120,000 men in Judah in one day.
All these men were strong and brave soldiers.
This happened because the people of Judah had abandoned the LORD.
The LORD is the God of their fathers.
passages.original: וַיַּהֲרֹג֩ פֶּ֨קַח בֶּן־ רְמַלְיָ֜הוּ בִּֽיהוּדָ֗ה מֵאָ֨ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֥ים אֶ֛לֶף בְּי֥וֹם אֶחָ֖ד הַכֹּ֣ל בְּנֵי־ חָ֑יִל בְּעָזְבָ֕ם אֶת־ יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י אֲבוֹתָֽם׃

passages.text: Zichri, a mighty man of Ephraim, killed Maaseiah the son of the king, Azrikam the governor of the palace, and Elkanah the second to the king.
passages.sermon:
Zichri was a mighty man from the tribe of Ephraim.
He killed Maaseiah.
Maaseiah was the son of the king.
Zichri also killed Azrikam.
Azrikam was the governor of the palace.
Zichri also killed Elkanah.
Elkanah was second to the king.
passages.original: וַֽיַּהֲרֹ֞ג זִכְרִ֣י׀ גִּבּ֣וֹר אֶפְרַ֗יִם אֶת־ מַעֲשֵׂיָ֙הוּ֙ בֶּן־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְאֶת־ עַזְרִיקָ֖ם נְגִ֣יד הַבָּ֑יִת וְאֶת־ אֶלְקָנָ֖ה מִשְׁנֵ֥ה הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ס

passages.text: Then the Israelites took 200,000 captives from their kinsmen—women, sons, and daughters. They also carried off a great deal of plunder and brought it to Samaria.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites attacked their own relatives from Judah.
They captured 200,000 people.
They took women, sons, and daughters as captives.
They also seized much plunder from them.
They brought all the plunder to Samaria.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁבּוּ֩ בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֨ל מֵֽאֲחֵיהֶ֜ם מָאתַ֣יִם אֶ֗לֶף נָשִׁים֙ בָּנִ֣ים וּבָנ֔וֹת וְגַם־ שָׁלָ֥ל רָ֖ב בָּזְז֣וּ מֵהֶ֑ם וַיָּבִ֥יאוּ אֶת־ הַשָּׁלָ֖ל לְשֹׁמְרֽוֹן׃ס

passages.text: But a prophet of the LORD named Oded was there, and he went out to meet the army that returned to Samaria. “Look,” he said to them, “because of His wrath against Judah, the LORD, the God of your fathers, has delivered them into your hand. But you have slaughtered them in a rage that reaches up to heaven.
passages.sermon:
A prophet of the LORD was there.
His name was Oded.
Oded went out to meet the army.
The army was returning to Samaria.
Oded spoke to them.
He said, “Look.
The LORD is the God of your fathers.
The LORD was angry with Judah.
Because of His anger, the LORD gave Judah into your hand.
But you killed them in great anger.
Your rage reached up to heaven.”
passages.original: וְ֠שָׁם הָיָ֨ה נָבִ֥יא לַֽיהוָה֮ עֹדֵ֣ד שְׁמוֹ֒ וַיֵּצֵ֗א לִפְנֵ֤י הַצָּבָא֙ הַבָּ֣א לְשֹׁמְר֔וֹן וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֗ם הִ֠נֵּה בַּחֲמַ֨ת יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֵֽי־ אֲבוֹתֵיכֶ֛ם עַל־ יְהוּדָ֖ה נְתָנָ֣ם בְּיֶדְכֶ֑ם וַתַּֽהַרְגוּ־ בָ֣ם בְזַ֔עַף עַ֥ד לַשָּׁמַ֖יִם הִגִּֽיעַ׃

passages.text: And now you intend to reduce to slavery the men and women of Judah and Jerusalem. But are you not also guilty before the LORD your God?
passages.sermon:
The Israelites captured people from Judah and Jerusalem.
They planned to make these men and women their slaves.
Oded was a prophet of the LORD.
He spoke to the Israelites.
He said, “You want to make your fellow Israelites slaves.
But you are also guilty before the LORD your God.”
passages.original: וְ֠עַתָּה בְּנֵֽי־ יְהוּדָ֤ה וִֽירוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ אַתֶּ֣ם אֹמְרִ֔ים לִכְבֹּ֛שׁ לַעֲבָדִ֥ים וְלִשְׁפָח֖וֹת לָכֶ֑ם הֲלֹ֤א רַק־ אַתֶּם֙ עִמָּכֶ֣ם אֲשָׁמ֔וֹת לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Now therefore, listen to me and return the captives you took from your kinsmen, for the fierce anger of the LORD is upon you.”
passages.sermon:
Oded was a prophet of the LORD.
Oded spoke to the army that returned to Samaria.
Oded said, "Listen to me now.
Return the captives you took from your own brothers.
The LORD is very angry with you."
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֣ה שְׁמָע֔וּנִי וְהָשִׁ֙יבוּ֙ הַשִּׁבְיָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר שְׁבִיתֶ֖ם מֵאֲחֵיכֶ֑ם כִּ֛י חֲר֥וֹן אַף־ יְהוָ֖ה עֲלֵיכֶֽם׃ס

passages.text: Then some of the leaders of the Ephraimites —Azariah son of Jehohanan, Berechiah son of Meshillemoth, Jehizkiah son of Shallum, and Amasa son of Hadlai—stood in opposition to those arriving from the war.
passages.sermon:
Some men were leaders of the tribe of Ephraim.
Their names were Azariah son of Jehohanan, Berechiah son of Meshillemoth, Jehizkiah son of Shallum, and Amasa son of Hadlai.
These leaders stood up.
They opposed the people who were coming back from the war.
passages.original: וַיָּקֻ֨מוּ אֲנָשִׁ֜ים מֵרָאשֵׁ֣י בְנֵֽי־ אֶפְרַ֗יִם עֲזַרְיָ֤הוּ בֶן־ יְהֽוֹחָנָן֙ בֶּרֶכְיָ֣הוּ בֶן־ מְשִׁלֵּמ֔וֹת וִֽיחִזְקִיָּ֙הוּ֙ בֶּן־ שַׁלֻּ֔ם וַעֲמָשָׂ֖א בֶּן־ חַדְלָ֑י עַל־ הַבָּאִ֖ים מִן־ הַצָּבָֽא׃

passages.text: “You must not bring the captives here,” they said, “for you are proposing to bring guilt upon us from the LORD and to add to our sins and our guilt. For our guilt is great, and fierce anger is upon Israel.”
passages.sermon:
The leaders of the Ephraimites spoke to those returning from war.
They said, “Do not bring the captives here.
If you do, you will bring guilt from the LORD upon us.
You will add to our sins and our guilt.
Our guilt is already great.
The LORD’s fierce anger is upon Israel.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ לָהֶ֗ם לֹא־ תָבִ֤יאוּ אֶת־ הַשִּׁבְיָה֙ הֵ֔נָּה כִּי֩ לְאַשְׁמַ֨ת יְהוָ֤ה עָלֵ֙ינוּ֙ אַתֶּ֣ם אֹמְרִ֔ים לְהֹסִ֥יף עַל־ חַטֹּאתֵ֖ינוּ וְעַל־ אַשְׁמָתֵ֑ינוּ כִּֽי־ רַבָּ֤ה אַשְׁמָה֙ לָ֔נוּ וַחֲר֥וֹן אָ֖ף עַל־ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס

passages.text: So the armed men left the captives and the plunder before the leaders and all the assembly.
passages.sermon: The armed men stood before the leaders and all the people.\r\nThey left the captives there.\r\nThey also left the plunder there.
passages.original: וַיַּעֲזֹ֣ב הֶֽחָל֗וּץ אֶת־ הַשִּׁבְיָה֙ וְאֶת־ הַבִּזָּ֔ה לִפְנֵ֥י הַשָּׂרִ֖ים וְכָל־ הַקָּהָֽל׃

passages.text: Then the men who were designated by name arose, took charge of the captives, and provided from the plunder clothing for the naked. They clothed them, gave them sandals and food and drink, anointed their wounds, and put all the feeble on donkeys. So they brought them to Jericho, the City of Palms, to their brothers. Then they returned to Samaria.
passages.sermon:
Certain men had been chosen by name.
These men stood up.
They took charge of the captives.
Some captives had no clothes.
The men gave clothing to the naked captives.
They used the plunder to provide these clothes.
They put clothes on the captives.
They gave sandals to the captives.
They gave food to the captives.
They gave drink to the captives.
They anointed the captives’ wounds.
Some captives were weak and could not walk.
The men put the weak captives on donkeys.
The men brought all the captives to Jericho.
Jericho is called the City of Palms.
They brought the captives to their brothers in Jericho.
After this, the men returned to Samaria.
passages.original: וַיָּקֻ֣מוּ הָאֲנָשִׁים֩ אֲשֶׁר־ נִקְּב֨וּ בְשֵׁמ֜וֹת וַיַּחֲזִ֣יקוּ בַשִּׁבְיָ֗ה וְכָֽל־ מַעֲרֻמֵּיהֶם֮ הִלְבִּ֣ישׁוּ מִן־ הַשָּׁלָל֒ וַיַּלְבִּשׁ֣וּם וַ֠יַּנְעִלוּם וַיַּאֲכִל֨וּם וַיַּשְׁק֜וּם וַיְסֻכ֗וּם וַיְנַהֲל֤וּם בַּחֲמֹרִים֙ לְכָל־ כּוֹשֵׁ֔ל וַיְבִיא֛וּם יְרֵח֥וֹ עִיר־ הַתְּמָרִ֖ים אֵ֣צֶל אֲחֵיהֶ֑ם וַיָּשׁ֖וּבוּ שֹׁמְרֽוֹן׃פ

passages.text: At that time King Ahaz sent for help from the king of Assyria.
passages.sermon:
King Ahaz ruled Judah.
At that time, King Ahaz needed help.
King Ahaz sent messengers.
He sent them to the king of Assyria.
King Ahaz asked the king of Assyria to help him.
passages.original: בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא שָׁלַ֞ח הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ אָחָ֛ז עַל־ מַלְכֵ֥י אַשּׁ֖וּר לַעְזֹ֥ר לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: The Edomites had again come and attacked Judah and carried away captives.
passages.sermon: The Edomites came again.\r\nThey attacked Judah.\r\nThey took captives from Judah.
passages.original: וְע֥וֹד אֲדוֹמִ֖ים בָּ֑אוּ וַיַּכּ֥וּ בִיהוּדָ֖ה וַיִּשְׁבּוּ־ שֶֽׁבִי׃

passages.text: The Philistines had also raided the cities of the foothills and the Negev of Judah, capturing and occupying Beth-shemesh, Aijalon, and Gederoth, as well as Soco, Timnah, and Gimzo with their villages.
passages.sermon:
The Philistines attacked Judah.
They raided cities in the foothills of Judah.
They raided cities in the Negev of Judah.
They captured Beth-shemesh.
They captured Aijalon.
They captured Gederoth.
They captured Soco and its villages.
They captured Timnah and its villages.
They captured Gimzo and its villages.
The Philistines lived in these places.
passages.original: וּפְלִשְׁתִּ֣ים פָּשְׁט֗וּ בְּעָרֵ֨י הַשְּׁפֵלָ֣ה וְהַנֶּגֶב֮ לִֽיהוּדָה֒ וַֽ֠יִּלְכְּדוּ אֶת־ בֵּֽית־ שֶׁ֨מֶשׁ וְאֶת־ אַיָּל֜וֹן וְאֶת־ הַגְּדֵר֗וֹת וְאֶת־ שׂוֹכ֤וֹ וּבְנוֹתֶ֙יהָ֙ וְאֶת־ תִּמְנָ֣ה וּבְנוֹתֶ֔יהָ וְאֶת־ גִּמְז֖וֹ וְאֶת־ בְּנֹתֶ֑יהָ וַיֵּשְׁב֖וּ שָֽׁם׃

passages.text: For the LORD humbled Judah because Ahaz king of Israel had thrown off restraint in Judah and had been most unfaithful to the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD humbled Judah.
Ahaz was king of Judah.
Ahaz led Judah to rebel against God.
Ahaz acted unfaithfully toward the LORD.
Because of Ahaz’s unfaithfulness, the LORD brought Judah low.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ הִכְנִ֤יעַ יְהוָה֙ אֶת־ יְהוּדָ֔ה בַּעֲב֖וּר אָחָ֣ז מֶֽלֶךְ־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּ֤י הִפְרִ֙יעַ֙ בִּֽיהוּדָ֔ה וּמָע֥וֹל מַ֖עַל בַּיהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Then Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria came to Ahaz but afflicted him rather than strengthening him.
passages.sermon:
Tiglath-pileser was the king of Assyria.
He came against Ahaz.
Tiglath-pileser oppressed Ahaz.
Tiglath-pileser did not help Ahaz.
Tiglath-pileser made Ahaz weaker, not stronger.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֣א עָלָ֔יו תִּלְּגַ֥ת פִּלְנְאֶ֖סֶר מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֑וּר וַיָּ֥צַר ל֖וֹ וְלֹ֥א חֲזָקֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Although Ahaz had taken a portion from the house of the LORD, from the royal palace, and from the princes and had presented it to the king of Assyria, it did not help him.
passages.sermon:
Ahaz was king of Judah.
Ahaz took treasures from the house of the LORD.
He took treasures from the royal palace.
He took treasures from the princes.
Ahaz gave these treasures to the king of Assyria.
The king of Assyria did not help Ahaz.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ חָלַ֤ק אָחָז֙ אֶת־ בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה וְאֶת־ בֵּ֥ית הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וְהַשָּׂרִ֑ים וַיִּתֵּן֙ לְמֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר וְלֹ֥א לְעֶזְרָ֖ה לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: In the time of his distress, King Ahaz became even more unfaithful to the LORD.
passages.sermon:
King Ahaz ruled Judah.
He faced great trouble.
During this time of distress, he acted.
He became even more unfaithful to the LORD.
He increased his wrongdoing against God.
passages.original: וּבְעֵת֙ הָצֵ֣ר ל֔וֹ וַיּ֖וֹסֶף לִמְע֣וֹל בַּיהוָ֑ה ה֖וּא הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ אָחָֽז׃

passages.text: Since Damascus had defeated him, he sacrificed to their gods and said, “Because the gods of the kings of Aram have helped them, I will sacrifice to them that they may help me.” But these gods were the downfall of Ahaz and of all Israel.
passages.sermon:
King Ahaz ruled over Judah.
Damascus defeated King Ahaz.
Ahaz sacrificed to the gods of Damascus.
Ahaz said, “The gods of the kings of Aram help them.
I will sacrifice to these gods.
Then they may help me.”
These gods did not help Ahaz.
These gods caused Ahaz to stumble.
These gods brought trouble to all Israel.
passages.original: וַיִּזְבַּ֗ח לֵֽאלֹהֵ֣י דַרְמֶשֶׂק֮ הַמַּכִּ֣ים בּוֹ֒ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר כִּ֠י אֱלֹהֵ֤י מַלְכֵֽי־ אֲרָם֙ הֵ֚ם מַעְזְרִ֣ים אוֹתָ֔ם לָהֶ֥ם אֲזַבֵּ֖חַ וְיַעְזְר֑וּנִי וְהֵ֛ם הָֽיוּ־ ל֥וֹ לְהַכְשִׁיל֖וֹ וּלְכָל־ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: Then Ahaz gathered up the articles of the house of God, cut them into pieces, shut the doors of the house of the LORD, and set up altars of his own on every street corner in Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
King Ahaz ruled in Judah.
Ahaz gathered all the articles from the house of God.
He cut the articles of the house of God into pieces.
He shut the doors of the house of the LORD.
He made altars for himself.
He set up these altars on every street corner in Jerusalem.
passages.original: וַיֶּאֱסֹ֨ף אָחָ֜ז אֶת־ כְּלֵ֣י בֵית־ הָֽאֱלֹהִ֗ים וַיְקַצֵּץ֙ אֶת־ כְּלֵ֣י בֵית־ הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים וַיִּסְגֹּ֖ר אֶת־ דַּלְת֣וֹת בֵּית־ יְהוָ֑ה וַיַּ֨עַשׂ ל֧וֹ מִזְבְּח֛וֹת בְּכָל־ פִּנָּ֖ה בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

passages.text: In every city of Judah he built high places to offer incense to other gods, and so he provoked the LORD, the God of his fathers.
passages.sermon:
Ahaz was king of Judah.
Ahaz built high places in every city of Judah.
He built these high places to offer incense to other gods.
Ahaz worshiped these other gods.
By doing this, Ahaz provoked the LORD.
The LORD is the God of Ahaz’s fathers.
passages.original: וּבְכָל־ עִ֨יר וָעִ֤יר לִֽיהוּדָה֙ עָשָׂ֣ה בָמ֔וֹת לְקַטֵּ֖ר לֵֽאלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֑ים וַיַּכְעֵ֕ס אֶת־ יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י אֲבֹתָֽיו׃

passages.text: As for the rest of the acts of Ahaz and all his ways, from beginning to end, they are indeed written in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
passages.sermon:
Ahaz was a king of Judah.
He did many things during his life.
He had many ways and actions, from the beginning to the end of his reign.
People wrote about all these things.
They wrote them in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
passages.original: וְיֶ֤תֶר דְּבָרָיו֙ וְכָל־ דְּרָכָ֔יו הָרִאשֹׁנִ֖ים וְהָאַחֲרוֹנִ֑ים הִנָּ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֔ים עַל־ סֵ֥פֶר מַלְכֵֽי־ יְהוּדָ֖ה וְיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: And Ahaz rested with his fathers and was buried in the city of Jerusalem, but he was not placed in the tombs of the kings of Israel. And his son Hezekiah reigned in his place.
passages.sermon:
Ahaz was a king of Judah.
Ahaz died.
People buried Ahaz in the city of Jerusalem.
They did not bury Ahaz in the tombs of the kings of Israel.
Hezekiah was the son of Ahaz.
Hezekiah became king after Ahaz.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֨ב אָחָ֜ז עִם־ אֲבֹתָ֗יו וַֽיִּקְבְּרֻ֤הוּ בָעִיר֙ בִּיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם כִּ֚י לֹ֣א הֱבִיאֻ֔הוּ לְקִבְרֵ֖י מַלְכֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ יְחִזְקִיָּ֥הֽוּ בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃פ
